question: Comparing the unilateral (1 tail) and bilateral hypothesis tests (2 tails):

options.opa: Bilateral tests always give higher p values.
options.opb: Bilateral tests always give lower p values.
options.opc: If a unilateral test is significant, so will the bilateral test.
options.opd: A bilateral test is more sensitive than a unilateral test.

analysis: In hypothesis testing, a bilateral (two-tailed) test considers both directions of an effect, while a unilateral (one-tailed) test considers only one direction. This means that for the same data, a bilateral test will generally have a higher p-value than a unilateral test because the significance level is split between two tails. Therefore, if a unilateral test is significant, it does not guarantee that the bilateral test will also be significant. Additionally, a bilateral test is not more sensitive than a unilateral test; in fact, it is less sensitive because it requires more extreme data to reach significance. Thus, the correct statement is that bilateral tests always give higher p-values than unilateral tests.
